title: The unit and counit of the derived adjunction u^{-1} -| Ru_* commute with the shift isomorphisms
statement:
Let $u:U	o V$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$ be the adjunction between $u^{-1}:\Dplus(V_{\Et})	o\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and $Ru_*:\Dplus(U_{\Et})	o\Dplus(V_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] on the bounded below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with unit $\eta^D_u:\mathrm{id}	o Ru_*u^{-1}$ and counit $\varepsilon^D_u:u^{-1}Ru_*	o\mathrm{id}$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction]. Write $[1]$ for the shift, $(M[1])^r=M^{r+1}$, $d_{M[1]}=-d_M$. Give $u^{-1}$ the shift-commutation isomorphism $\iota_M:u^{-1}(M[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(u^{-1}M)[1]$ which on a representing complex is the identity of the termwise shifted complex $u^{-1}(M^ ullet[1])=(u^{-1}M^ ullet)[1]$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], and give $Ru_*$ the shift-commutation isomorphism $\sigma_K:Ru_*(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(Ru_*K)[1]$ obtained by comparing the K-injective resolutions $K[1]	o I(K[1])$ and $K[1]	o I(K)[1]$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated], [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. Then for every $K\in\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ and every $M\in\Dplus(V_{\Et})$:

(a) (counit) $\varepsilon^D_{u,K[1]}=\varepsilon^D_{u,K}[1]\circ\iota_{Ru_*K}\circ u^{-1}(\sigma_K)$ as morphisms $u^{-1}Ru_*(K[1])	o K[1]$;

(b) (unit) $\sigma_{u^{-1}M}\circ Ru_*(\iota_M)\circ\eta^D_{u,M[1]}=\eta^D_{u,M}[1]$ as morphisms $M[1]	o(Ru_*u^{-1}M)[1]$.

That is, $\eta^D_u$ and $\varepsilon^D_u$ commute with the shift-commutation isomorphisms of the composite functors $Ru_*u^{-1}$ and $u^{-1}Ru_*$ (composites as in [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite]) and with the identity of $\mathrm{id}$, so that $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$ is an adjunction of triangulated functors; by iteration the same holds for the iterated isomorphisms $\iota^{(n)},\sigma^{(n)}$, $n\in\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: Use the existing proved upstream instance Adjunction.commShift_mapHomotopyCategory_unit from WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.MapDerivedCategoryAdjunctionShift. Its proof computes the termwise unit degreewise and descends through the homotopy quotient, so it gives shift compatibility for the homotopy-category unit for every integer shift.

Restrict the homotopy unit to the bounded below subcategory: under its faithful inclusion the unit is the homotopy-category unit composed with the canonical lift comparison isomorphisms. These isomorphisms, associators and unitors commute with shifts. NatTrans.CommShift.of_whiskerRight detects compatibility through the faithful inclusion. This calculation is the proved private helper plusHomotopyUnit_commShift.

Use Adjunction.derivedPlus_unit_app_fac to identify the derived unit after precomposition with Qh: it is Qh of the bounded below homotopy unit, followed by R.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit at L(K), then R.rightDerivedFunctorPlus of the inverse of L.mapDerivedCategoryPlusFactorsh. To prove this equality, postcompose with R.rightDerivedFunctorPlus of the forward exact-functor comparison, use derivedPlus_unit_app_fac, and cancel the inverse/forward comparison. The first factor commutes with shifts by the preceding step; the right-derived comparison commutes with its existing resolution-comparison shift structure by Functor.commShift_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit; the exact-functor comparison also commutes with its existing termwise shift structure. Whiskering and composition preserve compatibility. Since Qh is essentially surjective, apply NatTrans.CommShift.of_whiskerLeft using the inverse of its object-preimage isomorphism. This proves the private helper derivedUnit_commShift for arbitrary exact additive left adjoints with enough injectives on their target.

Apply derivedUnit_commShift to upperStarLowerStarAdjunction AddCommGrpCat f. The standard upstream sheaf Grothendieck-abelian instances supply enough injectives. Finally apply Adjunction.CommShift.mk' to the derived-unit compatibility. This proves compatibility of both unit and counit for every integer shift without transporting or replacing either functor's specified shift structure.
